items.title: Sharded remote pr-verification harness (test-efficiency workstream)
items.context: Lives entirely in the separate, fully user-owned pimmink/gsd-pi-ci harness repository, not in pimmink/gsd-pi — no upstream/fork PR is applicable. Adds .github/workflows/remote-pr-verification-sharded.yml, an experimental workflow_dispatch-only workflow that splits pimmink/gsd-pi's test:unit:compiled across 4 parallel shards using Node's native --test-shard=<index>/<total>, after independently validating locally (synthetic multi-glob fixture, exact production flag combination) that the flag must be placed before the glob patterns and is deterministic/complete/non-overlapping. Left the stable remote-pr-verification.yml completely untouched.
items.validation: Two real dispatches against pimmink/gsd-pi commit 28a2c92c3835e61f5fd19beffc6b8b4c6476bfc6 (fix/mai-cost-table-provider-section, historical GSD-W011/W014 spike commit, used only as a fixed measurement target). First dispatch (run 32015752880) failed fast and safely at an intentional file-count safety check (1274 actual vs an incorrectly hand-counted 1272 expected) before any shard ran. Corrective dispatch (run 32016308055) succeeded: all 4 shards + lifecycle-gate + aggregate green; aggregate totals across shards exactly matched the known unsharded baseline (14176 passed/0 failed/31 skipped), proving no test file was skipped or duplicated; total wall clock ~12m04s vs the 19m11s unsharded baseline (~37% reduction, run 31857969918). Merged to gsd-pi-ci:main (fast-forward, no PR needed for this private single-owner repo).
items.nextAction: None required to consider this workstream done. Optional future follow-up: consider promoting the sharded workflow from experimental to the primary remote-pr-verification path once used a few more times, and revisit shard_count if the real suite's size/composition changes materially.

items.title: Recovery artifact for GSD-W014 Phase I/J economics and routing spike
items.context: Not an independent feature or workstream. This is the recovery/provenance record for the stranded Phase-I/J spike commit e8e46fe9, which was built on top of the retired historical fix/mai-cost-table-provider-section branch (base fork main c4f78553, pre-1.16) rather than the clean feat/github-copilot-model-catalog-sync branch. Content is conceptually part of the GSD-W014 roadmap: provider-aware Copilot runtime economics (Phase I) in model-cost-table.ts and Copilot economics/drift handling in the copilot-models handler, plus router profile-confidence safety (Phase J) in model-router.ts, with accompanying tests. Because it sits on the wrong historical base it is not directly mergeable. The commit is archived on branch recovery/github-copilot-catalog-phase-i-j-e8e46fe9, pushed to origin at the same SHA.
items.validation: As of 2026-08-18: git show --stat reports 7 files changed, 615 insertions and 48 deletions; git show --check is clean; a secret/PII scan over the commit diff found only false positives (a runtime token variable and dummy 'token-abc' test fixtures), no real credentials. Ancestry: origin/fix/mai-cost-table-provider-section (28a2c92c) and d700abcf are ancestors of e8e46fe9; e8e46fe9 is NOT an ancestor of feat/github-copilot-model-catalog-sync or upstream/main; merge-base with upstream/main is c4f78553. Per-file divergence vs the committed catalog-sync branch: model-cost-table.ts and its test, model-router.ts and its test are Phase I/J content absent from catalog-sync; the copilot-models handler and its test diverged (Phase H parts superseded on catalog-sync, Phase I economics/drift unique to the spike); catalog.ts is largely superseded on catalog-sync. Local branch ref and origin remote ref both point to e8e46fe9450f326641fccf7bbf3929f10be80f09.
items.nextAction: Do not merge or cherry-pick wholesale. After the current GSD-W014 Phase-H working tree is committed and remotely verified, compare e8e46fe9 hunk-by-hunk against current upstream/main and reconstruct only the still-relevant, proven Phase-I/J pieces onto appropriate fresh upstream/main-based reviewable branches with their own scope, tests, and validation.
